newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends down sharply on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends down sharply on fund selling.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back sharply on Monday, pounded by heavy fund selling, trading sources said.
"The funds sold it down and wouldn't let up," one trader said. "They are getting out of December."
The downslide was led by the spot December contract, which slid a hefty 5.90 cents on the day -- or more than four percent -- to 119.95 cents, after ranging from 126.00 to 117.50.
Most-active March ended 2.75 cents lower, at 109.10, after ranging from 112.25 to 106.60. The back months closed down 0.75 to 2.40. The day's volume was brisk, at an estimated 10,315 lots.
The widely watched December/March switch narrowed to 10.85 cents, down from 14.00 cents at the close on Friday.

"It was a bit of a technical collapse," said Bill O'Neill, directer and senior futures strategist at Merrill Lynch. He noted the market started to stall at resistance on Friday, but when origin selling pressured prices this morning, touching off commission house sell-stops, the market quickly skid to the lows.
O'Neill said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report, which showed an increase in non-commercial long positions, also weighed on the market.
"The CFTC report showed a large increase in fund long positions," he said. "It was probably expected but it did make the market more vunerable."
The CFTC report showed non-commercial long positions rose by 1,113 lots in the two weeks ended November 5, to 6,986 lots, while non-commercial short positions fell by 491 lots, to 1,375 lots.
Commercial long positions increased by 389 lots in the two weeks, to 8,854 lots, and commercial short positions increased by 1,285 lots, to 18,436 lots.
Nonreportable long positions declined by 820 lots, to 10,924 lots and nonreportable short positions declined by 110 lots, to 6,953 lots.
On the charts, near-term support in the December contract was seen at 116.80, a low seen last week, with the next level noted at 114.00. March support was pegged at 107.00.

Fundamentally, O'Neill said the market would continue to focus on the tight stock situation in the near-term, but as the weeks go by and stocks begin to build there would be no compelling reason for the market to revisit last week's highs.
Low coffee inventories have buoyed the CSCE futures market, where prices rose last week to their highest levels since late August.

The tight supply situation resulted in part from a late harvest in Central America, where heavy rainfall took its toll on coffee-related infrastructure. A truckers' strike in Colombia last month also delayed deliveries of the 1996/97 crop to key consuming countries.

After the close Monday, the CSCE reported U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 471 60-kg bags in the week ended Nov. 8 to 333 bags -- or less than two lots of coffee, the lowest level since the exchange started tracking inventories in 1980.
The exchange said 1,200 60-kg bags of coffee were pending grading in its warehouses.
The spot December contract, which enters notice period on November 19, still has a relatively high open interest at 9,046 lots as of Friday -- the equivalent of more than two million bags of coffee.
